svg.title: Standardization changes the first principal component

cc:Work.dc:title: Standardization changes the first principal component
cc:Work.dc:description: PC1 explains 68.8% of variance in original units and 43.3% after standardization. Random blood glucose dominates the original-unit axis; urea, hemoglobin and creatinine have the largest absolute standardized coefficients.

g.text: Standardization changes the first principal component

text.style: font-size: 10.5px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #405460

g.text: Both fits use the same 400 median-imputed records and the same five measurements.

text.style: font-size: 9px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #405460

g.text: Standardization divides each centered measurement by its standard deviation. The sign of a whole PCA axis can be reversed.
